description: The Trade in Critical Minerals (TiCM) database brings together trade data, trade policies and visualisations for critical minerals such as lithium, cobalt and rare earth elements in one online tool. Bilateral trade and tariff data are given at the Harmonized System sub-heading level from the WTO Analytical Databases, and trade policies come from the WTO Trade Monitoring Database and the ePing trade measures platform, linked to HS codes. It was built by the Asian Development Bank and the WTO Secretariat and unveiled on 20 November 2024 at the COP29 conference in Baku. Coverage is global, and the data can be viewed online free of charge as bar charts, tree maps and network graphs of partners, product specialisation and trade networks. Caveats: the launch note is the only page read, because the database site could not be reached from the cloud session, so download options, years covered and licence are unverified. For simulation it supplies trade networks and policy measures for minerals needed by batteries, wind turbines and electric vehicles, useful for modelling supply chain disruption, export restrictions and resilience of the energy transition. It is related to the UNCTAD SDG Pulse critical minerals trade record in this catalogue, which maps a list of critical minerals to HS codes.
